dataset.name: real WANDS catalog (42,994 products), same 7 category_depth_1 checkpoints as P6A-E00/P6B-E00/P6C-E00

engine_config.lucene_facet_module: Apache Lucene 9.11.1 lucene-facet module (SortedSetDocValuesFacetCounts) via Maven Central, embedded Java harness (lucene-direct-bench/), NIOFSDirectory
engine_config.solr: Apache Solr 9.10.1, wands_bench core, re-queried same session

headline_result.correctness_gate: 8/8 filter and numeric-range counts exactly matched the live Solr wands_bench core in all 3 repeated runs; facet-sum-never-exceeds-candidates sanity check passed for module-based counts every run
headline_result.finding: substantially revises P6C-E00's own headline: Solr does not categorically outperform raw Lucene, it outperforms a naive per-candidate scan specifically -- Lucene's own specialized ordinal-based facet module reverses most of that gap, sharpening the facet-crossover finding into a claim about facet algorithms (naive scan vs. specialized ordinal-based counting), not generic-engine vs. commerce-native faceting in general
headline_result.newly_enabled_question: whether commerce-native's own facet_counts_by_scan could adopt an equivalent ordinal-based counting approach to close its own crossover -- untested, the single highest-value next question this phase surfaces
headline_result.named_limitation: only SortedSetDocValuesFacetCounts tested, not taxonomy-based faceting; no profiling of the mechanism; NIOFSDirectory not MMapDirectory; only WANDS 1x scale tested, not the Phase 6B scale ladder
